thread:
leo: thinking about tenant onboarding patterns again. two contenders: 1) operator-deployed agent that establishes an outbound mTLS tunnel to CP from the customer VPC, or 2) sidecarless regional relay where tenant traffic is routed into our regional endpoints. which way do we land on for long-term control-plane separation and safe rollbacks?

anya: agent wins for data residency and auditability. customer keeps egress control and we don't need to touch their route tables. downside: more moving parts for ops and users need to run something inside their account. :house_with_garden:

rachel: relay wins for developer velocity and uniform observability. onboarding becomes a config flip in CP rather than infra in customer account. downside: harder to preserve real client src ip and increases our attack surface.

infra-bot: Note: provisioning-job queued (onboard-spike/agent-vs-relay). healthcheck and perf probe will run automatically.

joel: two practical constraints: cert/key lifecycle and rollback story. With agent we can do customer-managed certs or CP-issued short-lived tokens. With relay we control keys centrally which helps rotations but less appealing to compliance customers.

leo: proposal sketch for agent mode: agent performs bootstrap with a signed one-time token (issued by CP), negotiates mutual TLS, posts a secure registration record (CP stores ephemeral endpoint). heartbeat every 30s. if heartbeat missing for 2 intervals, CP marks `prefers_relay=true` and flips routing until agent recovers. include an exponential backoff retry for restore.

anya: fallback semantics need to be explicit in headers/logs so support can say "switch to relay on X reason." maybe `x-rw-fallback-reason: heartbeat-missed` plus `x-rw-current-path: agent|relay`. Also, we should log the agent version to help triage.

rachel: also consider partial-fallback: some traffic classes (low-sensitivity) could go via relay while high-sensitivity stays stalled until agent recovers. config could be per-route.

leo: sample tenant config idea:
```
connect_mode: agent
bootstrap_token_expiry: 5m
heartbeat_interval: 30s
fallback: {
  policy: auto,
  ttl: 10m,
  split_routes: ["bulk-embeddings"]
}
```

joel: billing/egress note: agent scatters NAT addresses into customer accounts which inflates our NAT gateway costs and complicates per-tenant cost attribution. Could ask customers to attach a billing tag to their egress IPs or route egress via a shared transit account that we bill. Need to consult finance on metering plan.

anya: operational risk: more customer-managed infra means more support tickets blaming our agent; we should keep agent minimal (no ENI creation, only outbound allowed) and ensure safe uninstall.

leo: agree. spike plan: build a tiny agent that only opens outbound TLS, registers, emits heartbeat, and exposes a /health endpoint for local debug. No privileged networking changes. Measure: time-to-onboard (minutes), number of escalations in trial, and percent of traffic that needed fallback.

rachel: small rollout strategy: GA relay-by-default for self-serve tenants; offer agent-mode for enterprise/compliance customers behind a support cadence. That lets us keep the fast path while supporting isolation.

joel: action items: anya to draft header/logging schema and security notes; rachel to design telemetry metrics (agent_heartbeat_missed, fallback_rate, time_to_restore); leo to write a lightweight agent spec + bootstrap token format. reconvene next Tues.

anya: taking header schema. ETA Tue EOD.

leo: thanks all :thumbsup:
